cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to Israel, and they're about to go into the land they'll possess. He says the LORD will drive out many nations before them: the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.question: Moses names seven nations in the land. How does he say they compare to Israel?

answers.text: About the same size as Israel

cards.text: Moses says the LORD will deliver these nations over to Israel. And when He does, Israel must devote them to complete destruction.

cards.question: Moses says Israel may make a treaty with these nations.
No treaty and no mercy. Moses also tells Israel not to ___ with these nations.
Why does Moses tell Israel not to intermarry with these nations?

answers.text: They would turn Israel's sons away to serve other gods
They would claim a share of the land Israel was given
They would bring their armies right into Israel's camp

cards.text: Moses doesn't soften what comes next, either. The anger of the LORD would burn against Israel, and He would swiftly destroy them.

Then Moses gives Israel a to-do list for the altars, sacred pillars and Asherah poles in the land: tear them down, smash them, cut them down. Friend, that's not a to-do list, that's a whole DEMOLITION CREW!

cards.question: The altars, pillars and poles all come down. What does Moses tell Israel to do with the nations' idols?

answers.text: Bury them deep in the ground

cards.text: Then Moses tells them why, and it comes down to who Israel is. He says, "For you are a people holy to the LORD your God."

cards.question: The LORD has chosen Israel out of all the peoples on earth. What does Moses say they are to Him?
Moses says the LORD chose Israel because they outnumbered the other peoples.

cards.text: Moses says they were the fewest of all peoples. The FEWEST, friend! That's the three-person company getting picked for the biggest contract in town.

cards.question: So it wasn't their numbers. Moses says the LORD chose Israel because He ___ them and kept the oath He swore to their fathers.

cards.text: Love and a promise. That's why He brought them out with a mighty hand and redeemed them from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

cards.question: Moses calls the LORD the faithful God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion for those who love Him and keep His commandments.

cards.text: But Moses doesn't leave out the other side. Those who hate Him, the LORD repays to their faces with destruction, and He will not hesitate.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD keeps His covenant with those who love Him and repays those who hate Him. So what does Moses tell Israel to do?

answers.text: Keep the commandments he is giving them
Send spies ahead into the land first
Wait by the river for another sign

cards.text: Then Moses turns to what happens if Israel listens. If they keep these ordinances carefully, the LORD will keep His covenant and the loving devotion He swore to their fathers.

cards.question: Moses starts listing what the LORD will do for Israel. What does he say the LORD will bless?

answers.text: Their children and their land and their flocks
Their swords and their shields and their walls
Their tents and their tools and their wagons

cards.text: Grain, new wine and oil, the young of their herds and the lambs of their flocks. Moses says Israel will be blessed above all peoples, with no barren man or woman or livestock among them.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will remove all sickness from Israel.

cards.text: The terrible diseases Israel knew in Egypt won't be laid on them, Moses says, but on all who hate them. Then he comes back to the nations: Israel must destroy all the peoples the LORD delivers to them, and must not look on them with pity.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel not to worship the gods of these nations. What does he say worshiping them would be?

cards.text: Then Moses says what Israel may say in their hearts, like a boss answering your complaint before you even hit send: “These nations are greater than we are; how can we drive them out?”

cards.question: Moses tells Israel not to be afraid of these nations. Instead, they're to ___ what the LORD did to Pharaoh and all Egypt.

cards.text: The signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the outstretched arm. Moses says the LORD will do the same to all the peoples they now fear.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will also send something against these nations, until even the survivors hiding from Israel have perished. What is it?

cards.text: Don't be terrified by these nations, Moses says. The LORD is among Israel, and He is a great and awesome God.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will drive out these nations all at once.
Moses says the LORD will drive out these nations little by little. Why not all at once?

answers.text: The wild animals would multiply around Israel
Israel's army would grow too tired to fight
The land would be left without any farmers

cards.text: Friend, nobody wants to unpack the moving truck and find the neighborhood already claimed by something with CLAWS. But Moses says the LORD will give these nations over to Israel and throw them into great confusion.

cards.question: Moses says a few of these nations will still be able to stand against Israel.

cards.text: Their kings handed over, and no one able to stand against them. Then Moses comes to the images of their gods: Israel must burn them up.

cards.question: Moses warns Israel not to covet the silver and gold on the images of the nations' gods. What reason does he give?

answers.text: It is detestable to the LORD
It is owed to the kings

cards.question: Moses says not to bring any such thing into the house. Anyone who does will be set apart for ___, just like it.

cards.text: And that's where Moses leaves it for now, friend. Keep your apron on, because this man is NOT done preaching.
